 4 children, 2 adults hospitalized after police chase crash in Loganville
 By FOX 5 Atlanta Digital Team FOX 5 Atlanta Loganville Updated  November 16, 2026 3:14 PM EST Published  November 16, 2026 1:49 PM EST Share
 Copy Link 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Reddit 
 Updated  November 16, 2026 3:14 PM EST ▾ The Brief
 Four children and two adults went to area hospitals after a police chase ended in a crash on Georgia 10 West in Monroe. 
 Officers from three agencies pursued a stolen Hyundai Elantra before a Monroe police officer ended the chase near Georgia 81. 
 Investigators have not released the identities of the driver in custody or the exact conditions of the six people hospitalized. 
 LOGANVILLE, Ga. - A multi-agency police chase of a stolen car ended in a multi-vehicle crash near Monroe, sending four children and two adults to area hospitals Monday morning.
 What we know:
 The pursuit began when Monroe Police Department officers chased a vehicle into Loganville, according to Loganville Police Chief M.D. Lowry. 
 Georgia State Patrol troopers responded around 11:30 a.m. Monday to investigate a crash on Georgia 10 West near the intersection of Georgia 81, according to investigators.
 The Loganville Police Department was not involved in the pursuit.
 As the stolen Hyundai approached Georgia 81, the driver hit the back of a Nissan Altima before slamming into a Chrysler Pacifica, officials said.
 Officers stopped the fleeing vehicle on Highway 78 near Lee Byrd Road.
 A Barrow County sheriff's deputy then executed a precision immobilization technique, known as a PIT maneuver, to stop the pursuit. 
 Officers took the driver of the stolen Hyundai into custody at the scene. The driver was later identified as Andrea Crane, 38, of Athens. 
 Before the wreck, deputies from the Barrow County Sheriff's Office and Walton County Sheriff's Office joined City of Monroe police officers in pursuing a stolen Hyundai Elantra traveling on Georgia 10 West.
 Medical crews transported six people from the crash scene to area hospitals for treatment.
 Four children riding in the Chrysler Pacifica were taken to Children's Healthcare of Atlanta:
 A 4-year-old boy was airlifted to the hospital in critical condition. 
 A 2-year-old girl was transported by ground. 
 A 7-year-old boy was transported by ground. 
 A 9-year-old boy was transported by ground. 
 Ambulances also took two adults—the driver of the stolen Hyundai and the driver of the Nissan Altima—to Piedmont Walton Hospital.
 What we don't know:
 Authorities have not released the name of the driver taken into custody or the specific criminal charges they face.
 Investigators also have not shared the current medical conditions of the four children or the two adults hospitalized after the crash, nor have they said where the pursuit originally began.
 The Source: The information in this story was gathered from Loganville Police Chief M.D. Lowry, who reported the details of the pursuit and road closure, as well as Morris, who confirmed the child's medical transport. Additional information comes from the Georgia State Patrol.
